text:
A man was tired of living in his old house in the country and wanted to sell it and buy a better one. For several months, he tried to find a buyer on his own, putting up signs, talking to neighbours, and even putting it for sale in the small local newspapers, but nothing worked. No one seemed interested. At last, he decided to solve the problem by using an estate agent.

Within a few days, the estate agent placed an advertisement in a popular and expensive magazine, complete with a wonderful description of the house’s unique features including its peaceful surroundings, lovely gardens and other details that made the house sound almost like a dream house.

After the owner had read the advertisement, he hastened to telephone the estate agent and said to him, ‘I’m sorry, Mr Johns, but I’ve decided not to sell my house after all. After reading your advertisement in that magazine, I can see that it’s just the kind of house I’ve wanted to live in all my life.’
Note:
estate agent: means a person who helps sell or buy land, houses and buildings.
advertisement: means a notice telling people something is for sale.

text: Late one night, Mr Miller was woken up by a terrible noise in the street outside his house. It sounded as if a terrible fight was going on, and as Mr Miller loved nothing better than to watch a fight in the street, he opened his window and looked out. He saw two young men fighting just outside his front door, but when they saw him watching them, they went round the corner of the house and continued to shout at each other and to beat each other there. Mr Miller did not want to miss anything, so he ran down and opened his front door, but as it was a cold night, he wrapped himself in a blanket before he went out. He walked to the corner of his house looked round it. The two men were still shouting and struggling. Unaware of the fact that the men were acting, Mr Miller went closer to them, both to see the fight better and to try to find out what the men were fighting about. But as soon as he was within easy reach of the men, they stopped fighting, attacked him, seized his blanket and ran away into the darkness with it. Mr Miller was too old to run after them, so he could do nothing but go sadly back to bed without his blanket. ‘ Well, ’ said his wife. ‘ What were they fighting about? ’ ‘ It seems that they were fighting about my blanket, ’ answered Mr Miller, ‘ because as soon as they got it, their quarrel ended.’

Peter didn’t have money to pay his bills, so he always owed money to the shopkeepers in his town. Most of them didn’t ask for their money, but there was one who was not at all patient. Whenever this man saw Peter, he reminded him of the money that he had not yet paid him, and he argued about it in front of people, which made Peter feel very uncomfortable, as he did not want people to know that he was so poor. One day, therefore, Peter decided to teach the shopkeeper a lesson. The next time that the man stopped him in the street and began to shame him publicly about his debt to him, Peter said, “ Wait a minute. How much money do I owe you? ” “ You owe me exactly one hundred and twenty-two pounds.” answered the shopkeeper. “ Well, ” said Peter, “ If I paid forty pounds this month, another forty next month, and forty more the month after, how much would I still owe you? ” “ You would then owe me two pounds, of course.” answered the shopkeeper. “ Well, aren’t you ashamed of yourself, ” Peter said, “ giving me all this trouble for only two pounds? ”
